subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add a true soft-steer lifecycle that pauses or aborts active generation/tool work and resumes with injected user input, or should steer remain boundary-only with interrupt as the aborting mode?
rationale: Current main implements part of boundary steering, but the requested pause-or-abort/resume behavior changes runtime semantics, user expectations, and compatibility boundaries that code inspection cannot decide.

options.title: Define Soft-Steer Semantics
options.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers specify the accepted lifecycle, fallback, transcript, and backend behavior before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Boundary Steering
options.body: Treat the remaining actionable bug work as owned by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 and close or retitle this issue after preserving the broader discussion.

options.title: Reject Pause/Resume Mode
options.body: Leave steer as boundary-only, keep `/queue interrupt` as the aborting path, and document that true mid-stream pause/resume is not planned.

recommendation.title: Define Soft-Steer Semantics
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have maintainers specify the accepted lifecycle, fallback, transcript, and backend behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already posted the maintainer follow-up framing on this issue and is connected to the current active-run steering files by recent history.
